newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Supply ship docks with Russian Mir space station.
newsitem.headline: Supply ship docks with Russian Mir space station.

text.p: A supply ship docked with Russia's Mir space station on Monday, delivering equipment crucial for the future of the troubled 11-year mission, Mission Control said.
"Contact," a mission control official said amid applause in the control centre at Korolyov near Moscow.

Officials said the fully automatic docking operation would take six minutes from the first contact. They said the sprawling space station was directly over the Volga river in Russia on its orbit round the Earth when the docking took place.
The predecessor of the unmanned Progress craft launched on Saturday crashed into the station during docking on June 25 in the worst accident in the station's history.
Mir lost up to half its electric power in the collision and experts had said this could hamper Monday's docking.

The latest Progress craft is carrying oxygen, food and water as well as the tools needed to save the station. There are also parcels from the families of the three-man Russian-U.S. crew, who have had a nerve-wracking and uncomfortable time since the accident.
